title: Envelope on the filter
learned: One output can drive many inputs: one envelope shapes volume and colour
The ENV knob of the filter sets how far the envelope opens it
CUTOFF is where the sweep starts; the envelope adds on top
Short decay, low sustain and a filter envelope: the classic pluck and bass

steps.why: A plucked string is brightest at the moment it is hit and gets darker as it rings. A synth copies that by letting the envelope move the filter too, not only the volume.
steps.do: The notes from the last lesson play: clock → envelope → amplifier, through a filter that is set quite dark. Press Next.

steps.why: The filter has its own input for an envelope.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a second cable from ENV of the envelope to ENV of the filter.
steps.after: No change yet: the filter's ENV knob decides how much the envelope moves the cutoff, and it is in the middle, which means no change.

steps.why: Most inputs that change a knob have a small amount knob next to them. Here it is ENV in the MODULATION row of the filter.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn ENV of the filter to the right, more than halfway to the end.
steps.after: Every note now opens the filter and closes it again: a 'pew' or 'wow'. The envelope's 10 V moves the cutoff up by up to five octaves at full ENV.

steps.why: CUTOFF is where the filter rests; the envelope adds on top of it.
steps.do: Turn CUTOFF of the filter down a little and listen.
steps.after: The lower the cutoff, the darker the end of each note and the more the sweep stands out. Cutoff and envelope amount together set where each note starts and ends.

steps.why: Now make it a pluck: a short bright hit that dies away.
steps.do: On the envelope, turn SUSTAIN down near zero and DECAY short (to the left).
steps.after: Each note is a bright snap that turns dark and quiet at once: volume and colour fall together. This is the sound of countless synth basses and plucks.
steps.try: Turn ENV of the filter left of the middle: the envelope now closes the filter on each note instead of opening it. Then turn RESONANCE up for a squelchy bass.

steps.do: One envelope can drive as many things as you like. Press Next to finish.
